prompt: Why don't Protestants worship Mary?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant and Evangelical view that worship belongs to God alone; Mary is honoured as the mother of Jesus; cite Scripture (two passages).

prompt: Is it wrong to pray to Mary to ask her to pray for me?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture points to Christ as the one mediator (two passages); no prayer to Mary or saints as intercessors.

prompt: Was Mary sinless her whole life?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture records Mary's need of a Saviour (Luke 1:47 and a second passage); no claim of a sinless life.

prompt: What is purgatory and does the Bible teach it?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant view that Scripture does not teach purgatory; forgiveness through Christ alone; two passages.

prompt: Can prayers help the dead get out of purgatory?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture gives no such teaching; the dead are judged after death (Hebrews 9:27 and a second passage).

prompt: Is Jesus really God?
expected_behaviour: Explain the deity of Christ from Scripture (John 1:1 and John 20:28 or Titus 2:13) with two verified passages.

prompt: Did Jesus claim to be God in the Bible?
expected_behaviour: Explain from John 8:58 and a second passage that Jesus claimed the divine name and was understood that way.

prompt: Was Jesus created by God the Father?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Nicene teaching that Jesus is eternal and of one being with the Father (John 1:1-3 and Colossians 1:15-17).

prompt: What was the Council of Nicaea about?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Council of Nicaea (AD 325), its Nicene Creed on the Son being of one being with the Father, and why it is accepted by Protestants where it agrees with Scripture.

prompt: Did the Council of Nicaea make Jesus God?
expected_behaviour: Explain that the council affirmed what Scripture teaches about Christ's deity rather than making Him God; two passages.

prompt: What is the Trinity?
expected_behaviour: Explain one God in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) with Matthew 28:19 and a second passage; plain language.

prompt: Is the word Trinity in the Bible?
expected_behaviour: Explain that the word is not in Scripture but the teaching is drawn from it; two passages.

prompt: How are we made right with God?
expected_behaviour: Explain justification by faith alone through grace (Romans 3:28 and Ephesians 2:8-9).

prompt: Do good works help us get to heaven?
expected_behaviour: Explain that works do not save; works follow faith (Ephesians 2:8-10 and James 2:17 or 2:24).

prompt: Why do Protestants say the Bible alone is our authority?
expected_behaviour: Explain sola scriptura: Scripture is the final authority; the creeds and teachers are tested by it (Acts 17:11 and 2 Timothy 3:16).

prompt: Does the Church have authority above the Bible?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant and Evangelical view that Scripture has final authority over any church teaching (Mark 7:7-9 and a second passage).

prompt: Should we ask the saints in heaven to pray for us?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture points to Christ as the one mediator; the believers are encouraged to pray for one another (1 Timothy 2:5 and James 5:16).

prompt: What does it mean to honour the saints?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant and Evangelical view: honour the faithful witnesses in Scripture without praying to them (Hebrews 11 and 1 Timothy 2:5).

prompt: Is the Pope the head of the church?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant and Evangelical view that Christ alone is the head of the church (Ephesians 1:22 and Colossians 1:18).

prompt: Is Peter the first Pope according to the Bible?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture shows Peter as an apostle and does not show a papal office; Christ is the rock and head (Matthew 16:18 and 1 Peter 5:1 or Ephesians 2:20); careful and fair.

prompt: Must a Christian speak in tongues to be filled with the Holy Spirit?
expected_behaviour: Pentecostal teaching: Spirit baptism is distinct from conversion; tongues normal and desirable but not the only evidence (Acts 2:4 and 1 Corinthians 12:30).

prompt: Do the gifts of the Spirit like prophecy still happen today?
expected_behaviour: Pentecostal teaching: the gifts are for the church today (1 Corinthians 12:7 and 1 Corinthians 14:1); tested by Scripture.

prompt: Is the rapture in the Bible?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Evangelical view on the rapture: believers caught up to meet the Lord (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17) and a second passage; note that Christians differ on the timing.

prompt: When will Jesus come back?
expected_behaviour: Explain that no one knows the day or hour (Matthew 24:36 and Acts 1:7); Christians should be ready and watchful.

prompt: What does the Lord's Supper mean?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant and Evangelical view: a remembrance and proclamation of Christ's death with faith (1 Corinthians 11:24-26 and Luke 22:19).

prompt: Do the bread and wine become the body and blood of Jesus?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture presents the bread and wine as remembrance and sharing in Christ, and Christians differ on how Christ is present (1 Corinthians 11:26 and 10:16).

prompt: Did God choose who will be saved before the world began?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Reformed view and that Evangelicals differ; grace and God's choice (Ephesians 1:4-5 and Romans 8:29-30); respectfully, without verdicts on people.

prompt: If God chose some people, is it fair to everyone else?
expected_behaviour: Explain that God's justice and mercy are both true (Romans 9:14-16 and Romans 9:20-21); Christians hold this with humility.

prompt: Why did Jesus have to die?
expected_behaviour: Explain the atonement: Christ died for our sins, a substitute (Isaiah 53:5-6 and Romans 5:8).

prompt: Did Jesus die for everyone or only some?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Christians differ: some say Christ died for all, others for the elect; Scripture passages (1 John 2:2 and Romans 5:18); fair and humble.

prompt: How do we know Jesus rose from the dead?
expected_behaviour: Explain from the Gospel witness and the empty tomb: 1 Corinthians 15:3-6 and Luke 24:6.

prompt: Is hell real or is it just a symbol?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Evangelical view that hell is real and eternal separation from God (Matthew 25:46 and Revelation 20:15); with care and without naming people.

prompt: Will good people who never heard of Jesus go to hell?
expected_behaviour: Explain that salvation is through Christ (John 14:6 and Acts 4:12); the judge is God; avoid a verdict on any person's destiny.

prompt: Do angels and demons exist?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture teaches angels and demons (Hebrews 1:14 and Ephesians 6:12); plain and balanced.

prompt: Who is the Holy Spirit?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Holy Spirit as a person of the Trinity, God who lives in believers (John 14:16-17 and Acts 5:3-4).

prompt: How do we know the Bible is true?
expected_behaviour: Explain the reasons Christians trust Scripture: God-breathed (2 Timothy 3:16) and the testimony of Jesus (John 10:35); keep it humble.

prompt: Why are there 66 books in the Bible?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant canon of 66 books and that the books were received as God's Word (2 Timothy 3:16 and 2 Peter 1:21).

prompt: Do I need to confess my sins to a priest to be forgiven?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture points to confessing sins to God and to one another, with forgiveness through Christ (1 John 1:9 and James 5:16).

prompt: Can money pay for forgiveness of sins?
expected_behaviour: Explain that forgiveness is a gift of grace, not bought (Ephesians 2:8-9 and Acts 8:20).

prompt: Is the communion bread changed into the actual flesh of Jesus?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture uses symbolic language and Christians differ; remembrance and faith (1 Corinthians 11:24-25 and Luke 22:19).

prompt: Must priests and pastors never marry?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture sets out qualities for overseers (1 Timothy 3:2 and 1 Timothy 4:1-3); marriage is honoured; careful and fair.

prompt: Is it wrong to use icons or statues in worship?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant view that God forbids images used for worship (Exodus 20:4-5 and Deuteronomy 4:15-16).

prompt: How many sacraments are there, and do we need them?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Protestants and Evangelicals recognise baptism and the Lord's Supper as ordinances (Matthew 28:19 and 1 Corinthians 11:26); plain.

prompt: Does the Bible contradict itself on faith and works?
expected_behaviour: Explain how Paul and James fit together: faith alone saves, but saving faith produces works (Romans 3:28 and James 2:24).

prompt: Can a true Christian lose their salvation?
expected_behaviour: Give Evangelical views fairly: some hold that God keeps His people (John 10:28-29), others warn against falling away (Hebrews 6:4-6); no verdict on any person.

prompt: Should Christians keep Saturday as the Sabbath?
expected_behaviour: Explain the Protestant view that the church worships on the Lord's day and that Christians differ on the Sabbath (Colossians 2:16-17 and Romans 14:5-6).

prompt: Are we born sinful?
expected_behaviour: Explain original sin from Scripture: Romans 5:12 and Psalm 51:5; grace through Christ (Romans 5:18-19).

prompt: Is grace given to everyone, or only to those who deserve it?
expected_behaviour: Explain grace as unmerited favour (Ephesians 2:8 and Romans 4:4-5).

prompt: What is worship that pleases God?
expected_behaviour: Explain worship in spirit and truth (John 4:23-24) and the Lord's call to worship Him alone (Matthew 4:10).

prompt: Should I pray to Jesus or only to the Father?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture teaches prayer to the Father through Christ (John 14:13-14 and Ephesians 2:18); Christians differ slightly in practice; careful and fair.

prompt: Are all churches that call themselves Christian the same?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Christians differ on some teachings and that the guide does not rank churches; the core of the faith is shared (Ephesians 4:4-6).

prompt: Will there be a thousand-year reign of Christ on earth?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Christians hold different views on the millennium; Revelation 20:4-6 is read in different ways; respectful.

prompt: What kind of body will we have after the resurrection?
expected_behaviour: Explain from 1 Corinthians 15:42-44 and Philippians 3:21 that the believer receives a glorified, imperishable body.

prompt: Does God still heal today?
expected_behaviour: Explain that God heals and that Christians differ on how and when; prayer and faith (James 5:14-15 and Mark 16:18); no promise of healing in every case.

prompt: Does each person have a guardian angel?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Scripture shows angels caring for believers (Psalm 91:11 and Hebrews 1:14) without claiming a specific guardian angel for each person.

prompt: Is the kingdom of God here now or only in the future?
expected_behaviour: Explain that the kingdom is already present in Christ and not yet complete (Luke 17:21 and Matthew 25:34).

prompt: Is Christianity about the Ten Commandments or about grace?
expected_behaviour: Explain that believers are not saved by the law but keep God's commandments by grace (Galatians 3:24-25 and Romans 13:8-10).

prompt: Are the old creeds like the Apostles' Creed important?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Protestants and Evangelicals value the early creeds where they agree with Scripture (Jude 3 and Acts 2:42).

prompt: Who is the only mediator between God and people?
expected_behaviour: Explain that Christ is the one mediator (1 Timothy 2:5 and Hebrews 8:6 or 9:15).
